blocks.content: This is the complete contribution workflow. You already know every Git command in it — this chapter is about how they connect.
On GitHub, navigate to the repository and click Fork. GitHub creates a copy at github.com/your-username/project-name.

blocks.alt: GitHub repository page with the Fork button highlighted in the top-right corner

blocks.content: Your fork is now on your machine. You have full write access to it.
Work on a branch — not directly on main. This keeps your fork clean and your PR focused.
Step 4 — Make the change, commit, push

$ git add docs/example.md 
 $ git commit -m "Fix incorrect output in Python example"
 $ git push origin fix-broken-example
After the push, GitHub detects the new branch and shows a prompt at the top of your fork: "Compare & pull request." Click it.

blocks.alt: GitHub repository page showing the yellow banner prompting to compare and open a pull request after a recent push

blocks.content: 👉 Next, open and complete the pull request.
Use this space for your doubts about this lesson. Ask us anything that's confusing and our experts will provide explanations to help you understand.
